newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Heineken may buy Tempo stake. [CORRECTED 12:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Heineken may buy Tempo stake. [CORRECTED 12:40 GMT]

text.p: Israel's Tempo Beer Industries Ltd said on Tuesday that its controlling shareholders had reached an agreement aimed at turning Dutch brewer Heineken NV into a shareholder and strategic partner.

In a statement to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Tempo said Podhorzer Enterprises had granted an option to sell its 44.5 percent share in Tempo for $42 million to a shareholder group led by Jack Bar. The option is conditional on the shares being bought by Heineken within 90 days (corrects from 30 days), the statement said.

"Podhorzer Enterprises, which holds 44.5 percent of the share capital of Tempo, has granted irreversible option rights to purchase, as is, all these shares in return for a sum equal to $42 million to the Dutch company Heineken or other shareholders in Tempo from among the Bar and Bornstein families who will be required, if they exercise the option, to sell the shares to Heineken," the Tempo statement said.
Tempo, Israel's largest brewer and a leading maker of soft drinks, said the Bar-Bornstein group had told Tempo that it had begun negotiations with Heineken.
Company spokesmen were not immediately available to comment. The deal values Tempo at $96 million, which represents a 34 percent premium on the company's $70.4 million market valuation as of Monday.
